elements.name: intro_text
elements.html:
Thank you for your participation! Each video shows a person performing the described action in a 3D-scanned room. The study has two parts of 20 videos each and takes about 20 minutes.

Part 1: one motion per video; rate it from 1 (very poor) to 5 (excellent) on 3 questions.
Part 2: two motions side by side (1 = left, 2 = right); choose the better one for each of the 3 questions.

Please watch each whole clip before answering.

elements.name: participant__initials
elements.title: Please enter your name initials (e.g. XZ)

elements.name: part1_text
elements.html:
Part 1 of 2 · Rating. You will see 20 videos, each with ONE motion. Rate each motion from 1 (very poor) to 5 (excellent) on how well it follows the text, how physically plausible it is, and how natural and human-like it looks.

Please avoid the middle score 3 unless you really cannot lean either way: if a motion is somewhat good, give 4; if it is somewhat bad, give 2. Use the full range of the scale.

elements.html:

1 = very poor · 5 = excellent · please avoid 3 unless you truly cannot decide

elements.name: rate_physics__u01
elements.title: How physically plausible is the motion (no body parts passing through objects, no floating or sliding, no distorted or unnaturally twisted body)?

elements.name: rate_overall__u01

elements.name: part2_text
elements.html: Part 2 of 2 · Comparison. You will see 20 videos, each with TWO motions side by side (1 = left, 2 = right). For each question, choose the better motion. The shorter motion holds its last pose until the longer one ends.

elements.name: video_q01

elements.name: text__q01

elements.name: overall__q01
